 Monday Digest: Canadians Arriving in Form at Billie Jean King Cup
 By Pete Borkowski
 November 16, 2026
 Monday Digest 
 WTA 
 World Tennis 
 ATP 
 Momentum will certainly be at Team Canada's back heading into this week's Billie Jean King Cup play-off tie with Brazil.
 The top two Canadian singles players on the squad will both arrive in Vitoria fresh off titles. For one of them, their win was her third in her last four events.
 Here's what you need to know.
 Under the Radar: Andreescu, Cross, Kupres All Claim Titles
 Arguably no player in the world has been in better form over the last month than Bianca Andreescu.
 The 26-year-old arrived in Sopo, Colombia last week after having reached three WTA 125 finals in a row, winning the first two. The busy schedule may have been affecting her early as she dropped the first set of the tournament in the opening round against Rebeka Masarova but that was the only bump in the road for Andreescu, who did not drop another on her way to her third title in her last four WTA 125 events .
 Andreescu beat Elizabeth Mandlik 6-3, 6-3 in the final. The title in Sopo was the fifth in 2026 for the Canadian, the most professional singles titles she has won in a single year. With the win, she also vaults all the way up to No. 77 in the WTA rankings, well inside the cutoff for the main draw at January's Australian Open. She has climbed almost 100 spots in the rankings since the end of September, when she was ranked No. 172.
 Also as a result of this incredible four-event run from Andreescu, the Mississaugan currently sits tied for the most WTA 125 titles and has the outright lead for finals appearances with five in 2026.
 While Andreescu is expected to be Canada's No. 1 singles player at this week's Billie Jean King Cup Play-off tie against Brazil, the Canadian team's projected No. 2 singles player, Kayla Cross, will also be arriving in Vitoria fresh off a title.
 Cross reigned supreme at the W50 event in Chihuahua, Mexico last week. The Londoner was the top seed and did not drop a set on her way to the final. In the title match, she rallied from a set down to edge out Miriam Bianca Bulgaru 6-7(5), 7-5, 6-3 to secure her second singles title of the year.
 The 21-year-old also reached the doubles final in Chihuahua with Despina Papamichail, but the pair were beaten by Valeriya Strakhova and Anastasia Tikhonova.
 Critically, both Andreescu and Cross' titles came on outdoor clay, the same surface where this week's Billie Jean King Cup tie will be played. For Cross, the title in Chihuahua was her first career singles title on clay.
 Read also: ATP Finals Singles Round-Robin Preview - Debutants Look to Shine in Turin 
 Adding to the Canadian title parade last week was former NCAA star Mia Kupres, who won her first professional singles title at the M15 in Lincoln, Nebraska. The former national champion with Texas A&M dropped just one set, in the second round where she upset No. 8 seed Isabella Kruger, on her way to the title.  
 She secured her maiden singles title with a 6-2, 6-2 victory over Kristina Paskauskas. It was the fourth professional title overall for Kupres, who has three World Tennis doubles titles on her resume.
 Françoise Abanda had a chance to make it four Canadian titles last week, reaching the doubles final of the W15 event in Paris, but was beaten in straight sets.
 Canada played host to a M25 event in Montreal last week, but no Canadian's managed to reach the final. Twins Mikael and Nicolas Arseneault were the last Canadians standing in singles, both reaching the quarter-finals. Alexander Rozin got to the doubles semis. CLICK HERE for the full Montreal event recap.
 One last domestic event remains on the Canadian tennis calendar in 2026. Drummondville, QC, is hosting the Challenger Banque Nationale de Drummondville this week, an ATP Challenger event that will feature four of the five members of Canada's Davis Cup team for next week's Final 8 in Bologna, Italy, in action.
 The Birmingham National Wheelchair Tennis Championships took place last week in Vancouver, BC, with a number of familiar faces claiming the titles. Thomas Venos, Anne-Marie Dolinar, and Shawn Courchesne all doubled up, winning both the singles and doubles titles in their respective divisions.
 Venos took the men's singles and doubles with Barry Henderson, while Dolinar claimed the women's singles and doubles with Natalia Lanucha. Courchesne finished on top in the quad division, taking the doubles with Hisham Mohammed.
 CLICK HERE for the full Birmingham Nationals recap.  
 In Case You Missed It: Dabrowski Reaches WTA Finals Semis
 Gabriela Dabrowski and Luisa Stefani were red hot down the stretch on the WTA Tour, but they came up just short in their final event (as a team) of 2026.
 The top seeds at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells started off strong, going undefeated to finish atop Group 1 with wins over Hanyu Guo and Kristina Mladenovic , Su-Wei Hsieh and Jelena Ostapenko , and Elise Mertens and Shuai Zhang .  
 However, they were stumped in the semis by the eventual champions Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend , who took the spot in the final with a straight-set win.
 Click here for more news from the ATP and WTA Tours. 
 What to Watch: Canada Coming in Hot for Billie Jean King Cup
 One big event remains for Canada's women on the main tour and it is happening later this week in Vitoria, Brazil. Team Canada is heading south to take on the Brazilians in the Billie Jean King Cup Play-offs, with the winning nation getting back into the 2027 Qualifiers.
 Bianca Andreescu, Kayla Cross, Gabriela Dabrowski, Ariana Arseneault , and Clémence Mercier will be representing Canada. Laura Pigossi, Gabriela Ce, Luiza Fullana, Nauhany Vitoria Leme Da Silva, and Luisa Stefani form the host team.
 Andreescu beat Pigossi, who projects to be Brazil's No. 1 singles player, in straight sets on her way to the title in Sopo last week. There is also a high chance that Dabrowski and Stefani will find themselves across the net from each other in the doubles after their highly-successful 2026 season as a team.
 Matches will take place in Brazil on Friday and Saturday on outdoor clay.
 CLICK HERE for everything about the 2026 Billie Jean King Cup Play-off tie between Canada and Brazil.
